22661-clarimonde.title: Clarimonde
22661-clarimonde.creator: Unknown
22661-clarimonde.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. From my earliest childhood I had felt a vocation to the priesthood, so that all my studies were directed with that idea in view. Up to the age of twenty-four my life had been only a prolonged novitiate. Having completed my course of theology I successively received all the minor orders, and my superiors judged me worthy, despite my youth, to pass the last awful degree. My ordination was fixed for Easter week.

arxiv-1604-06575.title: Swift thermal steering of domain walls in ferromagnetic MnBi stripes
arxiv-1604-06575.creator: Alexander Sukhov, Levan Chotorlishvili, Arthur Ernst, Xabier Zubizarreta, Sergey Ostanin, Ingrid Mertig, Eberhard K. U. Gross, Jamal Berakdar
arxiv-1604-06575.description: Abstract We predict a fast domain wall (DW) motion induced by a thermal gradient across a nanoscopic ferromagnetic stripe of MnBi. The driving mechanism is an exchange torque fueled by magnon accumulation at the DWs. Depending on the thickness of the sample, both hot-to-cold and cold-to-hot DW motion directions are possible.

arxiv-1709-00111.title: Track 1 Paper: Good Usability Practices in Scientific Software Development Licensed under a CC-BY-4.0 license . DOI: 10.6084/m9.figshare.5331814.
arxiv-1709-00111.creator: Francisco Queiroz, Sandor Brockhauser, Raniere Silva, Jonah Miller, Hans Fangohr
arxiv-1709-00111.description: Abstract Scientific software often presents very particular requirements regarding usability, which is often completely overlooked in this setting. As computational science has emerged as its own discipline, distinct from theoretical and experimental science, it has put new requirements on future scientific software developments. In this paper, we discuss the background of these problems and introduce nine aspects of good usability.

arxiv-2012-14123.title: Spectral Analysis for Semantic Segmentation with Applications on Feature Truncation and Weak Annotation
arxiv-2012-14123.creator: Li-Wei Chen, Wei-Chen Chiu, Chin-Tien Wu † \dagger Department of Computer Science, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Hsin-Chu, Taiwan ‡ \ddagger Department of Applied Mathematics, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Hsin-Chu, Taiwanlwchen6309.cs07@nycu.edu.tw, walon@cs.nctu.edu.tw, ctw
arxiv-2012-14123.description: Abstract It is well known that semantic segmentation neural networks (SSNNs) produce dense segmentation maps to resolve the objects’ boundaries while restrict the prediction on down-sampled grids to alleviate the computational cost. A striking balance between the accuracy and the training cost of the SSNNs such as U-Net exists.

arxiv-2203-06722.title: Cloud Continents: Terraforming Venus Efficiently by Means of a Floating Artificial Surface
arxiv-2203-06722.creator: Alex R. Howe
arxiv-2203-06722.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alex R. Howe. The similarity of Venus and Earth in bulk properties make Venus an appealing target for future colonization. Several proposals have been put forward for colonizing and even terraforming Venus despite the extreme conditions on the planet’s surface. Such a terraforming project would face large challenges centered around removing Venus’s massive carbon dioxide atmosphere and replacing it with a habitable environment.

arxiv-2303-16713.title: Maximal operator in Hölder spaces
arxiv-2303-16713.creator: Piotr Michał Bies, Michał Gaczkowski, Przemysław Górka
arxiv-2303-16713.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Piotr Michał Bies, Michał Gaczkowski, Przemysław Górka. We study the maximal operator on the variable exponent Hölder spaces in the setting of metric measure spaces. The boundedness is proven for metric measure spaces satisfying an annular decay property. Let us stress that there are no assumptions on the regularity of the variable exponent and the variable exponent can touch values 0 0 and 1 1 . Furthermore, the continuity of the maximal operator between Hölder spaces is investigated.

arxiv-2309-03784.title: On the minimal simplex economy
arxiv-2309-03784.creator: Antonio Pulgarín
arxiv-2309-03784.description: Abstract In our previous paper we proved that every affine economy has a competitive equilibrium. We define a simplex economy as an affine economy consisting of a stochastic allocation (defining the initial endowments) and a variation with repetition of the number of commodities taking the number of consumers (representing the preferences).

arxiv-2404-04453.title: Constraints on Lepton Number Violation with the 2 tonne ⋅ \cdot yr CUORE Dataset
arxiv-2404-04453.creator: CUORE Collaboration † {}\dagger, ∗ Corresponding author: cuore-spokesperson@lngs.infn.it, † \dagger CUORE Collaboration authors and affiliations are listed in the supplementary materials.
arxiv-2404-04453.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by CUORE Collaboration † {}\dagger, ∗ Corresponding author: cuore-spokesperson@lngs.infn.it, † \dagger CUORE Collaboration authors and affiliations are listed in the supplementary materials.. Matter-antimatter asymmetry underlines the incompleteness of the current understanding of particle physics. Neutrinoless double-beta decay ( 𝟎 ​ ν ​ β ​ β \boldsymbol{0\nu\beta\beta} ) may help explain this asymmetry, while unveiling the Majorana nature of the neutrino. The CUORE experiment searches for 𝟎 ​ ν ​ β ​ β \boldsymbol{0\nu\beta\beta} of 130 Te using a tonne-scale cryogenic calorimeter operated at milli-kelvin temperatures.

arxiv-2406-08446.title: OLMES: A Standard for Language Model Evaluations
arxiv-2406-08446.creator: Yuling Gu, Oyvind Tafjord, Bailey Kuehl, Dany Haddad, Jesse Dodge Hannaneh Hajishirzi
arxiv-2406-08446.description: Abstract Progress in AI is often demonstrated by new models claiming improved performance on tasks measuring model capabilities. Evaluating language models can be particularly challenging, as choices of how a model is evaluated on a task can lead to large changes in measured performance.

arxiv-2408-12667.title: Gravitationally Misaligned Ultralight Dark Matter and Implications for Neutron Stars
arxiv-2408-12667.creator: Hooman Davoudiasl
arxiv-2408-12667.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hooman Davoudiasl. We examine the possibility that dark matter (DM) may be an ultralight scalar that was misaligned via non-minimal coupling to gravity, in the early Universe. For a certain regime of scalar masses, gravitational effects in neutron stars could place interesting bounds on the viable parameter space of the model, even in the absence of non-gravitational interactions between DM and ordinary matter. The dominant material in the Universe, generally referred to as dark matter (DM), is of unknown origin and character.

arxiv-2502-20683.title: Finite-momentum dielectric function and excitonic effects from time-dependent density-functional theory with dielectrically screened hybrid functionals
arxiv-2502-20683.creator: Didarul Alam, Jiuyu Sun, Carsten A. Ullrich
arxiv-2502-20683.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Didarul Alam, Jiuyu Sun, Carsten A. Ullrich. This paper studies the performance of time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) for calculating the dielectric function of semiconductors and insulators at finite momentum transfer, comparing against the standard Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE). Specifically, we consider a recently proposed hybrid approach that mixes dielectrically screened exact exchange with a semilocal functional, and we also introduce a new hybrid functional featuring a truncated dielectric screening scheme.

arxiv-2601-14994.title: Obscuring Data Contamination Through Translation: Evidence from Arabic Corpora
arxiv-2601-14994.creator: Chaymaa Abbas, Nour Shammaa, Mariette Awad
arxiv-2601-14994.description: Abstract Data contamination undermines the validity of Large Language Model evaluation by enabling models to rely on memorized benchmark content rather than true generalization. While prior work has proposed contamination detection methods, these approaches are largely limited to English benchmarks, leaving multilingual contamination poorly understood.

pmc-10512488.title: Sex steroid hormones and allergic diseases in children: a pilot birth cohort study in the Japan Environment and Children’s Study cohort
pmc-10512488.creator: Yumiko Miyaji, Kiwako Yamamoto-Hanada, Limin Yang, Mayako Saito-Abe, Miori Sato, Hidetoshi Mezawa, Minaho Nishizato, Masayuki Ochiai, Shouichi Ohga, Masako Oda, Hiroshi Mitsubuchi, Masayuki Shimono, Reiko Suga, Nathan Mise, Makiko Sekiyama, Shoji F. Nakayama, Yukihiro Ohya, the Japan Environment and
pmc-10512488.description: BackgroundNumerous studies suggest that sex steroids might play a role in sex disparity observed in allergic diseases in adults. However, whether sex hormones influence allergic diseases in children remains unclear. The aim of the present study was to examine the association of sex steroid hormones with allergic disease in Japanese children.

pmc-10726311.title: Impact of Restricted Phosphorus, Calcium-adjusted Diet on Musculoskeletal and Mental Health in Hypophosphatasia
pmc-10726311.creator: Katinka Kuehn, Andreas Hahn, Lothar Seefried
pmc-10726311.description: ContextImpairments in musculoskeletal and mental health are common in adults with Hypophosphatasia (HPP). Restricted phosphorus intake has been suggested to positively affect symptoms in HPP, but there is a lack of interventional evidence.ObjectiveThis work aimed to evaluate the effect of a phosphorus-restricted, calcium-adjusted diet on musculoskeletal and mental health in HPP.

pmc-12583112.title: Reconstruction of the Discourse on Influenza During Pandemics Between 1889 and 1980 in the Predecessor Journal of Swiss Medical Weekly - A Narrative Review and Bibliometric Analysis
pmc-12583112.creator: Natalija Radivojevic, Milo Puhan, Kaspar Staub, Tala Ballouz
pmc-12583112.description: ObjectivesUnderstanding how discourse surrounding influenza pandemics evolves over time can reveal shifts in scientific and public health priorities. This study reconstructs such discourse between 1889 and 1981 by identifying and comparing key research themes and trends in articles in predecessor journals of Swiss Medical Weekly (SMW).

pmc-12815758.title: Cigarette smoke exposure triggers dendritic cell-derived exosome-mediated Th17 and Treg polarization through an autophagy- and necroptosis-associated SIRT1-dependent mechanism in vitro
pmc-12815758.creator: Dongling Luo, Jifeng Liu, Leilei Ya, Chengxuan Ruan, Siyi Ou, Yiqian Wei, Qingyun Lin, Zhaohong Huang, Kaiwen Nong
pmc-12815758.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionBoth Th17/Treg cell imbalance and dendritic cells (DCs) play critical roles in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease pathogenesis from cigarette smoke. Previous studies have shown that DC-derived exosomes (DCexos) can polarize CD4+ T cells toward either Th17 or Treg phenotypes. However, the role of SIRT1 in regulating DCexos-mediated immune responses under cigarette smoke extract (CSE) exposure, and its association with autophagy and necroptosis, remains unclear.

pmc-12989190.title: Imidazole Alkaloids Epiisopilosine and Epiisopiloturine Attenuate Acetaminophen‐Induced Liver Toxicity in Mice via Autophagy Modulation and Anti‐Inflammatory Effects
pmc-12989190.creator: Ana Patricia de Oliveira, Gabriella Pacheco, André Luis Fernandes Lopes, Andreza Ketly da Silva Araujo, Letícia de Sousa Chaves, Simone de Araújo, Erick Bryan de Sousa Lima, Even Herlany Pereira Alves, Celso Martins Queiroz‐Junior, Mauro Martins Teixeira, Vivian Vasconcelos Costa, Jéssica Maria Tele
pmc-12989190.description: There is increasing interest in natural metabolites, such as alkaloids, due to their potential in treating liver diseases, including acetaminophen (APAP)‐induced hepatotoxicity. Alkaloids are known to modulate autophagy, a mechanism associated with liver protection. Epiisopilosine (EPIIS) and epiisopiloturine (EPI), imidazole alkaloids derived from Pilocarpus microphyllus (Jaborandi), exhibit anti‐inflammatory and hepatic immunomodulatory effects.

pmc-13002654.title: Nerve dissection technique to optimize functional outcome: resection of cystic vestibular schwannoma: how I do it
pmc-13002654.creator: Mohammed Hasen, Jihad Abdelgadir, Jeffrey Nadel, William T. Couldwell
pmc-13002654.description: BackgroundPreserving facial nerve function during the gross total resection of a cystic vestibular schwannoma (CVS) is a significant surgical challenge. In this paper we describe our technical strategy to achieve this objective.MethodA 59-year-old man with progressive left-sided hearing loss had a 2.9-cm partially cystic lesion in the left internal auditory canal (IAC) and cerebellopontine angle (CPA).

pmc-13223666.title: Weak economic evidence for WHO’s essential cancer medicines for Africa
pmc-13223666.creator: Aron E van der Steege, James Humuza, Cyprien Shyirambere, Hans Hogerzeil, Rob M P M Baltussen
pmc-13223666.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe WHO Model Lists of Essential Medicines (MLEM and MLEMc) guide national medicine selection, particularly in low-income and lower middle-income countries (LMICs). Concerns exist about the adequacy and transferability of economic evidence supporting recent cancer medicine additions.MethodsWe systematically examined modifications to cancer medicines on the WHO MLEM(c) between 2017 and 2023 and assessed their adoption into National Essential Medicines Lists (NEMLs) and NEMLs for children (NEMLcs) of African LMICs (2019–2024).

pmc-13233313.title: Neural representation of action symbols in primate frontal cortex
pmc-13233313.creator: Lucas Y Tian, Kedar Garzón Gupta, Daniel J Hanuska, Adam G Rouse, Mark A G Eldridge, Marc H Schieber, Xiao-Jing Wang, Joshua B Tenenbaum, Winrich A Freiwald
pmc-13233313.description: A hallmark of intelligence is proficiency in solving new problems, including those that substantially differ from previously seen problems. Problem solving in turn depends on the goal-directed generation of novel ideas and behaviours1, which has been proposed to involve internal representations of discrete units (or symbols) that can be recombined into numerous possible composite representations1–7.

pmc-13314335.title: Integrative analysis of semen quality and metabolomic profiles reveals breed-specific biomarker fertility in Indonesian buffalo
pmc-13314335.creator: Sigit Bintara, Kurniawan Dwi Prihantoko, Aeni Nurlatifah, Tulus Maulana, Athhar Manabi Diansyah, Sitti Nurhaliza, Rahmat Rahmat, Muhammad Fajar Amrullah
pmc-13314335.description: Background:The increasing demand for animal protein in Indonesia underscores the importance of improving the productivity of indigenous buffalo breeds, which remain underutilized. Semen quality plays a central role in the success of artificial insemination, and metabolomic profiling provides opportunities to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying fertility.

pmc-13356669.title: Construction and property characterization of PNIPAAm-grafted chitosan/sodium alginate composite Thermo-responsive hydrogel films
pmc-13356669.creator: Xiaoxue Lu, Jingna Liu, Yuanhong Zhuang, Bingli Wang, Peng Fei, Wenqiang Lai
pmc-13356669.description: A series of thermo-responsive PNIPAAm-CS/SA composite hydrogel films were synthesized via radical polymerization and ionic cross-linking. FTIR, XPS, and NMR confirmed the successful covalent grafting of PNIPAAm onto the chitosan (CS) backbone. XRD and SSNMR analyses revealed that the grafting disrupted the CS crystalline regions, inducing an amorphous structural transition.

pmc-13365968.title: IFPHOR0027 Improving the Inclusiveness of Data by Building Trust with Local Communities: The Coproduction of a Simple Guide to How We Use Your Data
pmc-13365968.creator: Neil Bendel
pmc-13365968.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Complete, accurate, up to date and consistently recorded data is essential for effective service planning, quality improvement and monitoring the equity of public services. The quality of data on ethnicity and other protected characteristics remains variable and there are known to be significant data gaps and inaccuracies among communities experiencing inequalities linked, in part, to a lack of understanding of, and mistrust in, how personal data is collected, managed and used among both local residents and staff groups.

pmc-13460016.title: Signals of Paleotemperature in the Age Structure and Seasonal Distribution of Pollination Syndromes Across a Temperate Region
pmc-13460016.creator: Thomas Leclère, Igor Bartish, Pille Gerhold, Andreas Prinzing
pmc-13460016.description: Across the planet, angiosperm diversification has been shaped by palaeoclimates and biotic interactions, particularly with pollinators, leaving signatures in the angiosperm age structure. Regional floras represent biased samples of this global diversification shaped by dispersal, extinction and environmental filtering, yet it remains unclear whether floristic age structure reflects pollination strategies or their interaction with palaeoclimates.

pmc-13501704.creator: Chi Zhang, Ye Liu, Yushan Zhang, Jie Zhang, Guoqing Fan, Zehong Huo, Dapeng Dai, Hong Shi, Ping Zeng, Ji Shen
